name: libaom AV1 (aomenc)
summary: aomenc is the command-line front end of libaom, the AOMedia reference AV1 encoder. It supports every AV1 profile (8/10/12-bit; 4:0:0, 4:2:0, 4:2:2 and 4:4:4) and exposes nearly every coding tool as a switch. Codec Wiki notes that it makes poor use of many threads in one process, so chunked encoding (for example with Av1an) is the usual way to parallelize it. HDR support is thin: it signals CICP color values but has no flags for mastering-display or content-light metadata, so HDR10 static metadata must be added at mux time.

hdr.summary: Encode at --bit-depth=10 (or 12 with profile 2) and set the three CICP flags: --color-primaries=bt2020, --transfer-characteristics=smpte2084 for HDR10/PQ or =hlg for HLG, and --matrix-coefficients=bt2020ncl. These are written into the AV1 sequence header. Color range is not a command-line flag: aomenc takes it from the Y4M header (XCOLORRANGE=FULL or LIMITED) and otherwise writes limited (studio) range. aomenc 3.15.3 has no options for mastering display color volume (MDCV) or MaxCLL/MaxFALL, and its WebM writer adds no Colour element, so for real HDR10 you have to add the static metadata when muxing, for example with mkvmerge --max-content-light, --max-frame-light, --chromaticity-coordinates, --white-color-coordinates, --max-luminance and --min-luminance. The CLI cannot carry HDR10+ dynamic metadata or Dolby Vision.
hdr.example: ffmpeg -i master.mov -pix_fmt yuv420p10le -strict -1 -f yuv4mpegpipe - | aomenc - --passes=1 --good --cpu-used=4 --end-usage=q --cq-level=20 --bit-depth=10 --input-bit-depth=10 --color-primaries=bt2020 --transfer-characteristics=smpte2084 --matrix-coefficients=bt2020ncl --threads=8 --row-mt=1 --ivf -o video.ivf && mkvmerge -o video.mkv --color-primaries 0:9 --color-transfer-characteristics 0:16 --color-matrix-coefficients 0:9 --color-range 0:1 --max-content-light 0:1000 --max-frame-light 0:400 --chromaticity-coordinates 0:0.680,0.320,0.265,0.690,0.150,0.060 --white-color-coordinates 0:0.3127,0.3290 --max-luminance 0:1000 --min-luminance 0:0.0001 video.ivf
pitfalls: HLG must be spelled --transfer-characteristics=hlg. The x265-style name arib-std-b67 is rejected and aomenc exits with its usage message (checked locally with 3.15.3). The numeric CICP code 18 also works because the parser accepts integers.
No MDCV or MaxCLL/MaxFALL flags exist. Without a muxer step the file is tagged PQ/BT.2020 but carries no static HDR10 metadata, and some players and TVs then fall back to guessed tone mapping.

The MaxCLL, MaxFALL and mastering values in the example are placeholders (P3-D65 primaries, 1000-nit mastering display). Copy the real values from the source with ffprobe or mediainfo; do not invent them.

--deltaq-mode=5 (HDR video) is mostly inert in 3.15.3: the per-block luma q offsets are compiled out (DISABLE_HDR_LUMA_DELTAQ is 1 in av1/encoder/encoder.h), so every block keeps the frame's base q. When the stream is exactly 10-bit with bt2020 primaries it still applies frame-level Cb/Cr delta-q offsets (av1/encoder/av1_quantize.c). Selecting it also replaces the default objective (TPL) delta-q mode 1.

Piping Y4M through stdin requires --passes=1. aomenc defaults to two passes in good-quality mode and reopens the input for pass 2, so stdin input gives an output that holds only a 32-byte IVF header (checked locally).
--full-still-picture-hdr refers to a full still-picture header, not high dynamic range. It has nothing to do with HDR.
--tune=butteraugli only accepts 8-bit input and is not compiled into the Homebrew build, so it cannot be used for HDR.

AV1 needs the Professional profile (2) for 12-bit or 4:2:2, and the High profile (1) for 4:4:4 at 8/10-bit. aomenc adjusts the profile to fit the input and prints a warning, in both directions (for example --profile=2 with 10-bit 4:4:4 Y4M becomes profile 1). Hardware decoders generally handle only profile 0.

Do not pass --profile=2 with 12-bit 4:2:2 or 4:4:4 Y4M input: aomenc 3.15.3 then stops with 'Failed to set chroma subsampling x: Unspecified internal error'. Leave --profile out (or at 0) and aomenc raises it to 2 itself. 12-bit 4:2:0 with --profile=2 works (all checked locally).
--chroma-sample-position applies only to 4:2:0. Set it to match the source. Many UHD HDR masters use top-left siting (AV1 colocated), but check before you set it.

presets.notes: Best compression libaom offers. Codec Wiki warns an encode at 0 could take weeks to finish. Use it only for tests or tiny clips.
Lumora's archival AV1 ladder ends its libaom rungs at 1 and 0. No source used here rates 1 against 0.
Codec Wiki: use if you have a lot of time. Good archival choice.
Codec Wiki: worth it for more efficiency than 4.
A step between Codec Wiki's balanced 4 and fast 6. Codec Wiki notes that SVT-AV1 handles only 4:2:0, so libaom is the AV1 option for 4:2:2/4:4:4 work.
Codec Wiki: choose 6 for speed. The help text lists 0..6 for good mode.
The library accepts up to 9 outside realtime mode, but the good-quality speed-feature tables stop at 6. Codec Wiki says speeds above 6 have the worst efficiency.
Realtime mode for low-latency or live encoding. From 7 up it uses non-RD mode, where delta-q modes 1-5 are silently ignored.
All-intra mode for still images and intra-only masters. Non-RD mode starts at 8.

rateControl.notes: Works like CRF in x264/x265. cq-level runs 0..63 and lower is better. Codec Wiki suggests 24 as a starting point. Lumora uses this mode with cq-level 14-40.

Uses cq-level as the quality target and also takes --target-bitrate. aomcx.h only states that cq-level applies in cq and q modes; how strictly the bitrate acts as a cap is not documented in the sources used here (unverified).
Default mode. Two-pass VBR is how libaom expects to be used for bitrate targets. Tune with --bias-pct, --minsection-pct and --maxsection-pct.
Constant bitrate for live or realtime use, normally together with --rt.
Mathematically lossless coding. Files are large. Valid at every bit depth and chroma format.
Bound the per-frame quantizer (0..63) in any mode.

options.description: Prints the option list and exits.
options.lumora: Lumora's Packager runs aomenc --help to check that the tool is installed.

options.description: Reads encoder settings from a config file instead of, or in addition to, command-line flags.
Debug mode. Makes output deterministic so runs can be compared byte for byte.
Output file. The container follows the extension: .ivf gives IVF, .obu gives raw OBUs, and anything else gives WebM unless another output flag overrides it.
options.lumora: Used as -o {out} with an .ivf extension.

options.description: Chooses the encoder. This build contains only the AV1 encoder.
Total number of encoding passes. Two passes collect first-pass statistics before the real encode. Three passes add an extra downscaled analysis pass.

recommendations.why: Each pass reopens the input. Stdin cannot be rewound, so the second pass sees no frames and the output holds only an IVF header (reproduced locally on a synthetic clip).
Codec Wiki says aomenc is designed around two passes to reach full efficiency. This needs a seekable input file.

options.lumora: Always --passes=1 (once): Lumora pipes Y4M on stdin, and aomenc's default of two passes in good mode would reopen the input.
options.notes: Listed twice in the help text (global and AV1 sections); it is one option. In aomenc.c the default is 2 for AV1 in good-quality mode. Realtime and all-intra modes force 1.

options.description: Runs only one pass of a multi-pass encode, so passes can be split across separate invocations that share --fpf.
Name of the first-pass statistics file that is written in pass 1 and read in pass 2.
options.notes: Needed when running --pass=1 and --pass=2 as separate commands.

options.description: Stops after encoding this many input frames.
options.notes: Handy for quick test encodes.

options.description: Skips this many frames at the start of the input before encoding.
Selects good-quality (offline) mode, the normal mode for file encoding. Same as --usage=0.
options.lumora: Not passed explicitly. Lumora relies on good mode being the default.
options.notes: In the library source, good mode is usage 0, the default.

options.description: Selects realtime mode for live or low-latency encoding. Forces a single pass and opens cpu-used 5..12.
options.notes: Turns off loop restoration and some other tools by default.

options.description: Selects all-intra mode, where every frame is a keyframe. Meant for still images (AVIF) and intra-only masters.

recommendations.why: libaom documents tune iq and ssimulacra2 as tuning modes for still and layered AVIF images, which are encoded in all-intra mode.

options.notes: Requires lag-in-frames 0 and kf-max-dist 0: the library rejects higher values in this mode. Several defaults change: QM min/max become 4/10 and screen detection mode 2.

options.description: Stops aomenc printing per-frame progress.
options.notes: Also hides the profile/bit-depth auto-upgrade warnings.

options.description: Prints the full encoder configuration before encoding. Useful for confirming which profile, bit depth and settings were actually used.

options.values: 0: disable, 1: PSNR at input bit-depth (default), 2: PSNR at stream bit-depth
options.description: Shows PSNR in the status line. Mode 2 measures at the coded bit depth, which only differs from mode 1 when input and stream depths differ.
options.notes: Off unless the flag is given.

options.default: WebM is the default when WebM IO is enabled
options.description: Writes a WebM container.
options.notes: aomenc's WebM writer does not write a Colour element or HDR mastering metadata. The bitstream CICP is still present.

options.description: Writes an IVF container, a minimal AV1 frame wrapper that mkvmerge, MP4Box and ffmpeg can remux.
options.lumora: Always passed; Lumora remuxes the IVF afterwards.

options.description: Writes a raw OBU (Section 5) stream with no container.
options.notes: Combine with --annexb=1 for Annex-B length-delimited output.

options.description: Prints a histogram of the quantizers used, grouped into the given number of buckets.
Prints a histogram of per-frame bitrates.
Hides the warnings about settings that may be wrong.
Still prints warnings but does not stop to ask whether to continue. Use it in scripts so a warning cannot hang the job.
Decodes each frame while encoding and checks that it matches the encoder's own reconstruction. Catches encoder/decoder mismatch bugs.
Treats raw input as NV12 (interleaved 4:2:0 chroma).
options.notes: Raw-input only; Y4M input carries its own format.

options.description: Treats raw input as YV12 (planar 4:2:0 with V before U).
options.notes: The 3.14.0 changelog deprecates the internal AOMYV12 image format; plain YV12 is still listed.

options.description: Treats raw input as I420 (planar 4:2:0).
Treats raw input as I422 (planar 4:2:2). AV1 needs profile 2 for 4:2:2.
options.notes: Raw-input only; Y4M 4:2:2 is detected automatically.

options.description: Treats raw input as I444 (planar 4:4:4). AV1 needs profile 1, or profile 2 at 12-bit.
Chooses the usage profile by number. The same thing as --good, --rt or --allintra.
options.notes: Library default is 0 (good).

options.description: Caps the number of worker threads. Effective use of threads needs row-mt, tiles or fp-mt.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki says aomenc largely lacks good multithreading and recommends Av1an for parallelism; its Av1an parameter set uses --threads=2 per chunk.

options.lumora: Passed as --threads={threads}: the cores one instance fills (cpuCores / instances for segments, cpuCores for a single encode). Measured at 1920x800, cpu-used 4: 2 threads kept 1.75 cores busy, 4 threads 2.36 and 8 threads 2.55, with the same output; more instances of fewer threads would use the CPU better, which 'Measure on this Mac' can find (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: Codec Wiki warns that above about 12 threads, still-image (AVIF) encodes can get slower.

options.description: AV1 bitstream profile. Main covers 8/10-bit 4:2:0 and mono. High adds 4:4:4 at 8/10-bit. Professional covers 12-bit and 4:2:2.

recommendations.why: The High profile is the lowest one that allows 4:4:4 below 12-bit.
Only the Professional profile allows 4:2:2. An explicit --profile=2 with 10-bit 4:2:2 Y4M encodes fine in 3.15.3 (checked locally).

aomenc raises the profile to 2 by itself for 12-bit input. An explicit --profile=2 with 12-bit 4:2:2 or 4:4:4 Y4M takes a different code path that fails in 3.15.3 with 'Failed to set chroma subsampling x' (checked locally).

options.lumora: Passed as --profile={aom_profile} from EncodeRecipes.aomProfile: 0 for 10-bit 4:2:0, 1 for 10-bit 4:4:4, 2 for 10-bit 4:2:2 and 12-bit 4:2:0, and 0 for 12-bit 4:2:2 and 4:4:4, which aomenc raises to 2 itself (an explicit 2 makes aomenc 3.15.3 exit with 'Failed to set chroma subsampling x'). Lumora therefore exports 12-bit 4:2:2 and 4:4:4 (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: aomenc adjusts the profile to fit the input format and bit depth and prints a warning (hidden by --quiet). It can lower it too: --profile=2 with 10-bit 4:2:0 input becomes 0, and with 10-bit 4:4:4 becomes 1. Library default is 0.

options.description: Frame width for raw input. Y4M input supplies this itself.
Frame height for raw input.
options.notes: The short form is -h, not help. Use --help to get help.

options.description: Writes a larger maximum frame width into the sequence header than the actual frames use, so the resolution can grow later in the stream.
options.notes: Spelled with underscores, unlike most flags.

options.description: Height counterpart of --forced_max_frame_width.
Labels the WebM output as stereoscopic 3D with the given frame packing. Only affects WebM metadata.
Sets the timestamp precision in the output.
options.notes: The help footer states the 1/1000 default.

options.description: Stream frame rate. Y4M input supplies it; raw input needs it.
Turns on error-resilience features for the whole stream, so decoding can recover after lost packets.
options.notes: Pointless for file-based delivery.

options.description: Bit depth of the coded stream. 10-bit is the minimum for HDR. 12-bit requires profile 2.

effect.size: often smaller at 10-bit for the same quality

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki recommends 10-bit for everything: less banding and usually smaller files, even from 8-bit sources.
12-bit keeps the master's full precision. It needs the Professional profile, which few hardware decoders support.

options.lumora: Passed as --bit-depth={bits} (10 or 12 on the AV1 Pro path).
options.notes: If --input-bit-depth is higher, aomenc raises --bit-depth to match and warns. Library default is 8.

options.description: The actual bit depth of the input samples, which can differ from the coded depth (for example 8-bit input coded as 10-bit).
options.lumora: Passed as --input-bit-depth={bits}, the same as --bit-depth. The Y4M Lumora pipes in must therefore be at that depth.
options.notes: Y4M headers carry the depth. A mismatch can garble the picture or trip --validate-hbd-input.

options.description: How many future frames the encoder buffers before deciding on the current one. Longer lookahead helps alt-ref placement, temporal filtering and rate control.

recommendations.why: 48 is the highest value 3.15.3 accepts. Anything above it is refused when the encoder starts (checked locally).
Codec Wiki recommends 64 and says higher values bring little. On 3.15.3 that value fails with 'g_lag_in_frames out of range', so the two sources disagree. Use 48.

options.notes: Library default in good mode is 35. All-intra mode forces 0.

options.description: Large-scale tile mode for special uses such as light-field or VR tile streaming, where single tiles are decoded independently.
options.notes: Turns off film grain options. Ordinary players cannot use it.

options.description: Encodes luma only (4:0:0) and drops the chroma planes. Good for black-and-white material.
options.notes: Allowed in every profile.

options.description: Writes the full sequence header rather than the reduced one for still pictures. HDR here means header, not high dynamic range.
options.notes: Often mistaken for an HDR option. It is not one.

options.description: Forces the high-bit-depth (16-bit) internal pipeline even for 8-bit encodes.
options.notes: Turned on automatically whenever --bit-depth is above 8.

options.description: Writes the bitstream in Annex-B length-delimited format, normally together with --obu.
Lets the encoder drop frames when the rate-control buffer falls below this fullness, to hold a bitrate.
options.notes: Realtime/CBR use. Library default is 0 (off).

options.description: Encodes frames at a lower resolution, scaled back up after decoding (reference scaling). Dynamic mode reacts to bitrate pressure.
options.notes: Unverified: mode 2 (random) appears intended for testing.

options.description: Scale factor for fixed resize mode. The frame is scaled by 8 divided by this value.
options.notes: The range comes from the library's scale numerator of 8; the help does not state it.

options.description: Like --resize-denominator, but for keyframes.
AV1 super-resolution. Frames are coded at reduced width, then upscaled horizontally and restored inside the loop. Can save bits at very low bitrates.

effect.quality: - at normal rates, ± at very low

options.notes: Rarely worth it for high-quality encodes. Not supported with --timing-info=model.

options.description: Horizontal downscale factor (8 divided by this value) for fixed superres mode.
Superres denominator for keyframes.
In qthresh superres mode, superres is used only for frames whose qindex is above this threshold.
options.notes: Library default is 63.

options.description: Keyframe version of --superres-qthresh.
options.notes: Library default is 32.

options.description: Rate-control mode. q is constant quality (CRF-like), cq is quality-targeted under a bitrate cap, vbr targets an average bitrate and cbr a constant one.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki uses q with cq-level, which behaves like CRF in x264/x265.

aomcx.h says cq-level is used in both cq and q modes. cq is the constrained-quality mode (aom_encoder.h) and also takes --target-bitrate; how hard that bitrate caps the result is not documented in the sources used here.

options.lumora: Always --end-usage=q.
options.notes: Library default is vbr. The 3.15.0 changelog mentions a force-max-q option for VBR, which does not appear in this aomenc help.

options.description: Target bitrate in kilobits per second for vbr, cbr and cq.
options.notes: Ignored in q mode. Library default is 256 kbps.

options.description: Best (lowest) quantizer that rate control may use.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Worst (highest) quantizer that rate control may use. Lowering it guards against ugly frames in hard scenes.
options.notes: Library default is 63.

options.description: How far below the target bitrate rate control may go before it reacts.
options.notes: Library default is 25.

options.description: How far above the target bitrate rate control may go.
options.notes: Library default is 25.

options.description: Size of the decoder buffer model in milliseconds, used by CBR/VBR.
options.notes: Library default is 6000.

options.description: Buffer fullness the model assumes at the start.
options.notes: Library default is 4000.

options.description: Buffer level that rate control tries to stay near.
options.notes: Library default is 5000.

options.description: In two-pass VBR, controls how far bits move from easy to hard sections. 0 spreads bits evenly; 100 follows complexity fully.
options.notes: Library default is 50.

options.description: Lowest bitrate a GOP section may get in two-pass VBR, as a percentage of the target.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Highest bitrate a GOP section may get in two-pass VBR.
options.notes: Library default is 2000.

options.description: Allows forward keyframes. These are random-access points coded like alt-refs that can still reference earlier frames, which is cheaper than a full keyframe.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki turns it off when Av1an handles scene cuts and keyframes.

options.notes: Library default is 0. (Unverified: some demuxers and players are reported to seek poorly to forward keyframes.)

options.description: Minimum spacing between keyframes.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Maximum spacing between keyframes, which limits how far a player may need to seek back.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki leaves keyframe placement to Av1an's scene detection.

options.notes: Library default is 9999. For standalone files that need quick seeking, about 10 seconds of frames is a common choice, but no source used here specifies a value.

options.description: Turns off automatic keyframe placement. Only the first frame is a keyframe.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki uses it because every Av1an chunk already starts at a scene cut.

options.notes: Never use it on a whole film encoded in one piece: the result would be almost unseekable.

options.description: Interval for switch frames (S-frames), which let adaptive-streaming clients switch between renditions.
options.notes: Library default is 0 (off).

options.description: Chooses how S-frames are inserted.
options.notes: The 3.10.0 changelog says the sframe_mode field is not implemented, so it may have no effect.

options.values: 0..6 in good mode, 5..12 in realtime mode, 0..9 in all intra mode
options.description: Main speed/efficiency control. Lower numbers search more and compress better but take far longer.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki's recommended value.
Codec Wiki suggests 2 if you have plenty of time, and 3 for a bit more efficiency than 4.
Codec Wiki suggests 6 for speed and warns that higher values have the worst efficiency.
The good-quality speed-feature tables stop at 6, so 7-9 in good mode add little beyond 6 even though the library accepts them.

options.lumora: Passed as --cpu-used={preset}. The AV1 Pro ladder runs 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (measured on an M3 Max, CPU time per frame relative to 6 / size saved against 6: 5 0.82 / 3%, 4 0.40 / 15%, 3 0.26 / 17%, 2 0.099 / 22%); the archival AV1 ladder adds libaom rungs 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 measured against SVT-AV1 (cpu-used 4 at 0.033 of preset 10's speed, about as small as preset 1). The encoders.json default is 4 (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: Library default is 0 in good mode, which is extremely slow, so always set it.

options.description: Allows hidden alternate reference frames: filtered future frames that many frames predict from. A core libaom efficiency tool.
options.notes: Library default is 1. Leave it on.

options.description: Blocks whose motion error is below this threshold are skipped as static. Faster but can freeze fine changes.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Row-based multithreading inside each tile. The main way libaom uses more cores without tiles.

recommendations.why: It is the library default and is needed for good thread use without tiles.

options.lumora: Always --row-mt=1.

options.description: Frame-parallel multithreading: encodes several frames of a GOP at once for more speed on many-core CPUs.
options.notes: Unverified: the library is said to fall back to normal threading for configurations it cannot run frame-parallel, and output can differ from fp-mt=0.

options.description: Splits the frame into 2 to the power N tile columns, which can be encoded and decoded in parallel at a small efficiency cost.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki advises no tiles at 1080p or lower.
Codec Wiki suggests one level of tile columns at 1440p.
Codec Wiki suggests 2 tile columns and 1 tile row at 2160p for decode and encode parallelism.

options.notes: Library default is 0. The value is log2: 2 means 4 columns.

options.description: Splits the frame into 2 to the power N tile rows.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki's 4K suggestion, used with tile-columns=2.
Codec Wiki advises no tiles at these sizes.

options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Temporal dependency model. Estimates how much each block is referenced later and gives heavily used areas more bits.

recommendations.why: It is the default and --deltaq-mode=1 requires it, according to the help text and the codec control docs.

options.notes: aomcx.h gives the default as 1 and says the control is left out of realtime-only builds.

options.values: 0: no filter, 1: filter without overlay (default), 2: filter with overlay - experimental, may break random access in players
options.description: Applies the temporal (ARNR) filter to keyframes, removing noise before coding them.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki picks 1. Mode 2 is more efficient but has seeking problems and FFmpeg cannot read it.

options.description: How many neighboring frames the alt-ref temporal filter averages.
options.notes: Library default is 7.

options.description: Strength of the alt-ref temporal filter. Higher values denoise more, which helps compression but can smear grain, texture and line art.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki suggests 1 for 3D/CGI-like and 2D animation, where strong temporal filtering harms flat areas and lines.
Codec Wiki suggests 4 for live action, and possibly higher at low bitrates.

options.lumora: Not set (library default 5). 1 saved under 1% on CG and anime* and cost faces 3.4%; 3 saved under 0.7% (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: Library default is 5 (av1_cx_iface.c). Codec Wiki describes 4 as the default, which does not match the 3.15.3 source.

options.values: psnr, ssim, vmaf_with_preprocessing, vmaf_without_preprocessing, vmaf, vmaf_neg, butteraugli, vmaf_saliency_map, iq, ssimulacra2
options.description: Chooses which quality metric rate-distortion decisions optimize for. psnr is the library default. The vmaf modes need libvmaf and a model file. iq and ssimulacra2 are perceptual modes built for still images.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki recommends ssim, and suggests setting it explicitly in case defaults change.

aomcx.h describes tune=iq as an image-quality mode guided by SSIMULACRA 2 and subjective checks, meant for still or layered AVIF images. It turns on QM (qm-min 2, qm-max 10), sharpness 7, dist-metric qm-psnr, adaptive CDEF, chroma delta-q, Variance Boost, screen detection mode 2 and adaptive sharpness.
The 3.15.3 header says iq and ssimulacra2 are not recommended for video, but the 3.14.0 changelog says both now work in good-quality and realtime modes. Supported is not the same as recommended.
tune=butteraugli rejects input above 8-bit. The Homebrew build also lacks it and errors out (checked locally).

options.lumora: Not set (psnr). tune=ssim was 5-24% larger at equal VMAF though 1-10% smaller at equal XPSNR; tune=iq was 33-62% larger (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: Lumora never sets --tune for aomenc, so it runs at psnr. vmaf* modes look for the model at /usr/local/share/model/vmaf_v0.6.1.json by default, which does not exist with Homebrew on Apple silicon; pass --vmaf-model-path. ssimulacra2 uses hand-made heuristics and does not call the metric itself.

options.description: Quality level for q and cq modes. Lower values give higher quality and larger files.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki's example value. It behaves like CRF, so adjust by eye or by a target metric.

options.lumora: Passed as --cq-level={quality}. Lumora's target-quality search runs between 14 (best) and 40 (worst).
options.notes: Library default is 10. It is ignored in vbr and cbr.

options.description: Caps keyframe size as a percentage of the average frame budget. Mainly for CBR and streaming.
options.notes: Library default is 0 (no cap) in good mode.

options.description: Caps the size of inter frames as a percentage of the average.
Extra bits for golden frames in CBR mode.
options.notes: CBR only.

options.description: Mathematically lossless coding.
options.notes: Works at 8/10/12-bit and every chroma format. Lossy settings such as cq-level and film grain do not apply.

options.values: 0: false, 1: true (default), 2: disable for non-reference frames, 3: enable adaptively based on frame qindex
options.description: Constrained Directional Enhancement Filter, an in-loop deringing filter that follows edge direction.
options.notes: tune=iq and tune=ssimulacra2 switch to 3 (adaptive).

options.values: 0: false (default in realtime mode), 1: true (default in non-realtime mode)
options.description: Loop restoration (Wiener and self-guided filters) that restores detail after deblocking and CDEF.
Allows rectangular block splits (horizontal and vertical halves).
Allows AB partitions: three-way splits that combine a half with two quarters.
Allows 1:4 and 4:1 strip partitions.
Smallest block size the partition search may use. Raising it speeds up encoding but loses fine detail.
options.notes: The help says 4K and above, or faster speeds, force a minimum of 8. Library default is 4.

options.description: Largest block size the partition search may use.
options.notes: Library default is 128.

options.description: Allows separate horizontal and vertical interpolation filters for motion compensation.
Lets the encoder use a different quantizer offset for chroma than for luma, which usually gives chroma more bits.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki lists it as a free efficiency gain from testing. tune=iq turns it on too.

options.lumora: Not set. It moved BD-rate by under 0.3% for 3-18% more time (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).

options.description: Smooths the neighboring edge pixels used for directional intra prediction.
Writes frame order hints so the decoder knows frame distances. Several compound and temporal-MV tools depend on it.
options.notes: Turning it off also turns off distance-weighted compound and ref-frame MVs.

options.description: Allows 64-point transforms for large smooth areas.
Allows the extended transform types: flipped ADST, identity and one-dimensional transforms. Identity transforms help with sharp synthetic edges.
Allows rectangular transform sizes.
Distance-weighted compound prediction, which weights two references by their temporal distance.
Master switch for masked compound prediction (wedge and difference-weighted).
Allows compound prediction from two references on the same temporal side.
Blends an inter prediction with an intra prediction inside one block.
Smooth-blend variant of inter-intra prediction.
Compound prediction weighted by the difference between the two predictors.
Wedge-shaped masks that combine two inter predictions.
Wedge masks for inter-intra blending.
Frame-level global motion models (pans, zooms, rotations) for camera movement.
Local warped motion, which fits affine motion per block from neighboring motion vectors.
Recursive filter-based intra prediction modes for textured blocks.
Smooth intra prediction modes for gradients.
options.notes: Matters for banding-prone gradients such as HDR skies.

options.description: Paeth intra predictor, which picks the closest of the top, left and top-left neighbors.
Chroma-from-luma prediction, which predicts chroma from the reconstructed luma. Especially useful at 4:4:4.
Diagonal directional intra modes (D45 to D203). Has no effect when directional intra is off.
Uses video coding settings even when the input is a single frame.
Overlapped block motion compensation, which blends neighboring block motion to soften block edges.
Codes overlay frames, which show the real frame at an alt-ref's position after the filtered alt-ref.
Palette prediction mode for blocks with few distinct colors, such as UI, text and flat animation.
options.notes: Allowed by default, but the encoder only tries screen tools when its screen detector or --tune-content=screen says so.

options.description: Intra block copy, which copies already-coded areas of the same frame. Very effective on repeated text and UI.
options.notes: Only used when screen content tools are active. It turns off in-loop filters for that frame.

options.description: Fine angle steps for directional intra prediction.

options.values: 0: false 1: true 2: true for rd search 3: true for estimate yrd search (default)
options.description: Controls where trellis (rate-distortion-optimized) coefficient quantization is skipped. The default skips it only in an estimation step.
options.notes: The logic is inverted: 0 means trellis is used everywhere.

options.description: Uses frequency-weighted quantization matrices, which spend fewer bits on high frequencies the eye notices less.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki lists it as a free efficiency gain from testing. tune=iq turns it on too.

options.lumora: Offered as the optional 'Quantization matrices' option (--enable-qm=1) on the AV1 Pro and archival libaom rungs, but no longer recommended for any content type: it was larger at equal XPSNR on every tuning clip (+0.8% to +5.8%) and 4-16% slower (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).

options.description: Lowest (steepest) QM flatness level the encoder may pick. Lower means more frequency weighting.
options.notes: Only matters with --enable-qm=1. tune=iq sets 2. The 3.12.0 changelog changed the all-intra defaults.

options.description: Highest (flattest) QM level the encoder may pick. 15 is flat, meaning no weighting.
options.notes: tune=iq sets 10.

options.description: Uses a smaller set of transform types, signaled in the bitstream. Faster encode and simpler decode, at some efficiency cost.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Restricts intra blocks to DCT transforms.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Restricts inter blocks to DCT transforms.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Uses only the default transform type for each intra mode, with no search.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Uses an adaptive variant of the block quantizer.
options.notes: Library default is 0. Little public guidance.

options.values: 0: SB, 1: SB Row per Tile, 2: Tile, 3: Off
options.description: How often coefficient cost tables are refreshed during the search. Less often is faster but less accurate.
options.notes: Library default is 0 (per superblock).

options.values: 0: SB, 1: SB Row per Tile, 2: Tile, 3: Off
options.description: Update frequency for mode cost tables.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.values: 0: SB, 1: SB Row per Tile, 2: Tile, 3: Off
options.description: Update frequency for motion-vector cost tables.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Turns on bitstream features that let decoders work on frames in parallel, mainly by turning off backward context adaptation.
options.notes: Not the same as --fp-mt, which is encoder threading.

options.description: Per-frame error-resilience mode for lossy networks.
Segment-based adaptive quantization. Variance mode gives flat areas more bits; cyclic refresh is meant for realtime.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki says 0 is usually better but notes that this is debated and some users prefer 1.

options.values: 0: off, 1: deltaq objective (default), 2: deltaq placeholder, 3: key frame visual quality, 4: user rating based visual quality optimization, 5: HDR video, 6: Variance Boost
options.description: Changes the quantizer per superblock. Mode 1 follows the TPL model for objective gains, modes 3 and 4 target perceptual quality, mode 5 is labeled HDR video, and mode 6 (Variance Boost) protects low-variance areas.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki found 0 more perceptually efficient. This disagrees with the library default of 1, which aims at objective metrics.

recommendations.value: do not expect per-block HDR tuning from 5
recommendations.why: In 3.15.3 the per-block HDR luma offsets are compiled out (DISABLE_HDR_LUMA_DELTAQ 1), so mode 5 keeps every block at the base q. At exactly 10-bit with bt2020 primaries it still lowers chroma q through frame-level Cb/Cr offsets, and choosing it turns off the default mode 1.
Variance Boost was added for all-intra in 3.12 and extended to good-quality and realtime modes in 3.14. tune=iq turns it on.

options.lumora: Not set (default 1). 0, 5 (HDR, on PQ clips) and 6 (variance boost) were all larger, by 1-18% (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: Modes 1-5 are silently ignored in non-RD mode (cpu-used 8 and up in all-intra, 7 and up in realtime). Mode 1 requires --enable-tpl-model=1.

options.description: Scales how strong delta-q modulation is for modes 4 and 6.
options.notes: Library default is 100.

options.description: Lets deblocking filter strength vary per superblock along with delta-q.
options.notes: Has no effect when deltaq-mode is 0.

options.description: Periodically lowers q on some frames to lift quality.
options.notes: Unverified: mainly used in realtime encoding.

options.description: Turns on the temporal denoiser (luma only) used by realtime and SVC encoding. It is not part of film grain synthesis.
options.notes: Library default is 0. In 3.15.3 source it is only used in the realtime/SVC denoiser path, so it probably does little in good mode.

options.description: Tells the encoder what kind of content it has. screen turns on screen-content tools (palette, intra block copy) for every frame. film turns on film grain synthesis using a fixed built-in grain pattern.

effect.quality: screen: + on UI/text; film: adds synthetic grain

recommendations.why: Forces screen-content tools and intra block copy instead of leaving it to automatic detection.

recommendations.value: avoid film unless you want generic grain
recommendations.why: In 3.15.3, film writes the same synthetic grain parameters into every frame (one luma scaling point, no measurement of the source) and enables film grain in the sequence header.

options.lumora: The screen tune adds --tune-content=screen. On Lumora's screen clip it produced the same stream as automatic screen detection (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: There is no 'animation' value in libaom. Library default is default.

options.values: 0: no CDF update, 1: update CDF on all frames (default), 2: selectively update CDF on some frames
options.description: Controls whether the entropy coder's probability tables adapt from frame to frame.

options.values: bt709, unspecified, bt601, bt470m, bt470bg, smpte240, film, bt2020, xyz, smpte431, smpte432, ebu3213
options.description: CICP color primaries written to the sequence header. It labels the stream and does not convert pixels.

recommendations.why: HDR10 and HLG both use BT.2020 container primaries. bt2020 is the spelling aomenc accepts.

options.lumora: Passed as --color-primaries={cp_name}, from encoders.json colorNames: bt2020 for pq/hlg and bt709 for sdr.
options.notes: Library default is unspecified. smpte432 is P3-D65 and smpte431 is DCI-P3.

options.values: unspecified, bt709, bt470m, bt470bg, bt601, smpte240, lin, log100, log100sq10, iec61966, bt1361, srgb, bt2020-10bit, bt2020-12bit, smpte2084, hlg, smpte428
options.description: CICP transfer function written to the sequence header. smpte2084 marks PQ (HDR10) and hlg marks Hybrid Log-Gamma.

recommendations.why: The CICP name for the PQ curve in aomenc's list.
aomenc spells HLG 'hlg'. 'arib-std-b67' is not in its list and makes aomenc exit (checked locally).

options.lumora: Passed as --transfer-characteristics={tc_name}: smpte2084 for HDR10, hlg for HLG (checked: tagged arib-std-b67 in the stream), bt709 for SDR.
options.notes: Library default is unspecified. Integer CICP codes are also accepted (16 = PQ, 18 = HLG).

options.values: identity, bt709, unspecified, fcc73, bt470bg, bt601, smpte240, ycgco, bt2020ncl, bt2020cl, smpte2085, chromncl, chromcl, ictcp, ipt-c2, ycgco-re, ycgco-ro
options.description: CICP matrix coefficients (how Y'CbCr relates to R'G'B'), written to the sequence header.

recommendations.why: BT.2020 non-constant luminance is the matrix used by HDR10 and HLG. bt2020ncl is aomenc's name for it.

options.lumora: Passed as --matrix-coefficients={mc_name}: bt2020ncl for pq/hlg and bt709 for sdr.
options.notes: identity means RGB coding, which needs 4:4:4. ictcp is for ICtCp sources.

options.description: Signals where 4:2:0 chroma samples sit. vertical means left-sited (MPEG-2 style); colocated means top-left, co-sited with luma.

effect.quality: none (signaling; wrong value shifts chroma by half a pixel on display)

options.notes: Only applies to 4:2:0. Library default is unknown. Set it to the source's siting.

options.description: Minimum golden-frame / alt-ref group length.
options.notes: The library rejects values above 47 (MAX_LAG_BUFFERS minus 1).

options.description: Maximum golden-frame / alt-ref group length. Longer groups help static content.

effect.size: smaller for static content when longer

options.notes: The library rejects values above 47 (MAX_LAG_BUFFERS minus 1), and a non-zero value must be at least 2 and at least --min-gf-interval.

options.description: Minimum depth of the hierarchical frame pyramid within a GF group.
Maximum depth of the hierarchical frame pyramid. Deeper pyramids compress better.
Superblock size. dynamic lets the encoder choose 64x64 or 128x128 depending on resolution and speed.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki recommends dynamic so both 128x128 and 64x64 are available.

options.notes: Library default is dynamic.

options.description: Maximum number of tile groups (OBU packets carrying tiles) per frame.
options.notes: For packetized network delivery.

options.description: Sizes tile groups to fit a network MTU. Overrides --num-tile-groups.
Writes timing info, and optionally a decoder model, into the bitstream.
options.notes: The help says model only works with no hidden frames and no superres. Library default is unspecified.

options.description: Applies one of 16 built-in test grain parameter sets. Meant for conformance testing, not for matching real footage.
Loads film grain parameters from a table file, from libaom's noise_model or photon_noise_table tools or another estimator, instead of estimating grain internally.

effect.size: smaller if the source was denoised

recommendations.value: table from photon_noise_table (with -t smpte2084 or hlg for HDR)
recommendations.why: The tool models sensor shot noise from an ISO value and resolution and supports PQ and HLG transfers, so grain scales correctly in HDR. photon_noise_table is a libaom example program; the Homebrew aom package installs only aomenc and aomdec (checked locally).

recommendations.value: table from noise_model (noisy source vs. denoised source)
recommendations.why: On Doom9, a user built a table from the difference between the source and an externally denoised copy, then encoded the denoised copy. Another poster said this has real advantages over coding the grain, but the user noticed the grain pattern repeating when the video was paused.

options.lumora: Offered as 'Grain measured from this film (libaom)' on the archival ladder: --film-grain-table={grain_table}, with a table Lumora measures itself.
options.notes: A grain table does not denoise anything by itself: denoising only runs when --denoise-noise-level is above 0, which defaults to 0. Feed an already denoised source, or the real grain is coded and the synthetic grain is added on top. Large-scale-tile mode ignores the table.

options.description: Turns on libaom's internal noise model. It estimates the grain, writes AV1 film grain parameters, and (by default) denoises the frame before coding so the decoder adds the grain back.

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki uses 8 and warns that above 12 the grain starts to look patterned.
A Doom9 user found that raising it gave artificial-looking noise and that the built-in denoiser was heavy-handed.

options.lumora: Offered as 'Film grain synthesis' on both libaom ladders at level 4, but no longer recommended, and the encoders.json grain tune no longer adds it: on heavy grain, low light and old anime* it was 3-26% larger at equal VMAF and XPSNR than coding the grain, against both the de-grained master and the noise-free original, at every level from 4 to 16, and 15-35% slower. When used, ExportEngine now scores it with the synthetic grain stripped (docs/encoding/tuning-aomenc.md).
options.notes: Library default is 0 (off). Lumora's 10 is inside Codec Wiki's limit of 12 but above its suggested 8.

options.description: Block size the noise model uses to find flat areas and estimate grain.
options.notes: No public tuning guidance found.

options.description: Controls whether the frame is actually denoised when denoise-noise-level is on. With 0, grain is still estimated and synthesized, but the source grain is coded as well.

effect.quality: 0 keeps more real texture but adds synthetic grain on top

recommendations.why: Codec Wiki turns off the built-in denoiser when using grain synthesis because it removes too much.
Codec Wiki suggests keeping denoising on for very noisy sources.

options.lumora: Not set (default 1).
options.notes: Lumora leaves it at the default (1), so its denoise-noise-level option both denoises and synthesizes.

options.description: Maximum number of reference frames each frame may use.
Restricts the single and compound reference combinations the encoder searches.
Temporal motion-vector prediction from reference frames.
options.notes: Needs order hints.

options.values: ABxy: AB = operating point index, xy = level index (e.g. 0 = level 2.0 for OP 0, 1019 = level 6.3 for OP 10)
options.description: Asks the encoder to stay within a given AV1 level for an operating point, which limits bitrate, tiles and picture size for device compatibility.
options.notes: Pair with --strict-level-conformance=1 to make violations fatal.

options.values: 32-bit mask; bit 0 = Main tier (default), 1 = High tier
options.description: Chooses Main or High tier for each of the 32 operating points. High tier allows higher bitrates per level.
Keeps each frame's compression ratio above a floor, mainly to satisfy level limits.
Assumed average complexity per macroblock for single-pass VBR with lookahead, used to spread bits.
options.notes: Only for one-pass VBR.

options.description: Horizontal chroma subsampling of raw input. Used to describe 12-bit raw input in profile 2.
options.notes: For 12-bit Y4M input, aomenc takes subsampling from the Y4M header and ignores this.

options.description: Vertical chroma subsampling of raw input.
VMAF model file used by the vmaf tune modes.

recommendations.why: The built-in path /usr/local/share/model/vmaf_v0.6.1.json does not exist there, so vmaf tunes abort without this flag (checked locally).

options.notes: VMAF models are trained on SDR content, so vmaf tunes are a questionable target for HDR.

options.values: 0: SB, 1: SB Row per Tile, 2: Tile, 3: Off
options.description: Update frequency for displacement-vector (intra block copy) cost tables.
options.notes: Only matters when intra block copy is active.

options.description: Folder where partition decisions are read or written, for research and analysis tools.
options.notes: Library default is '.'.

options.description: Master switch for directional intra prediction modes.
options.notes: Turning it off also makes --enable-diagonal-intra irrelevant.

options.description: Searches for the best transform size per block. When off, the largest transform that fits is always used.
options.notes: Ignored in realtime non-RD mode.

options.values: 0: Loopfilter disabled for all frames, 1: Enable loopfilter for all frames (default), 2: Disable loopfilter for non-reference frames, 3: Disable loopfilter for frames with low motion
options.description: Controls when the deblocking filter runs.
options.notes: Options 2 and 3 are speed features, mostly for realtime.

options.description: In all-intra mode, automatically turns off some intra tools where they are unlikely to help.
options.notes: Only active with --deltaq-mode=3. Library default is 0.

options.description: Guides per-block delta-q from an external rate distribution map.
options.notes: Needs --deltaq-mode=3 and --rate-distribution-info.

options.description: Input file with the rate distribution map for --enable-rate-guide-deltaq.
options.notes: Library default is ./rate_map.txt.

options.description: Picks tools that are cheaper to decode, for weak playback devices. Supported for good-quality speeds 1-3 at 608p-1080p vertical and 720p-1080p horizontal.
options.notes: Development was marked complete for VOD in 3.15.0. Not meant for 4K.

options.description: In three-pass encoding, where the output of the first two passes goes.
options.notes: Only for --passes=3. If it is not given, aomenc names the file <output>_pass2_<n>.ivf.

options.description: Log file written by the second pass, used by the third pass.
Places forward keyframes at a fixed interval.
options.notes: Needs --enable-fwd-kf=1.

options.description: With 1, the encoder stops instead of producing a stream that breaks the target level.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Tries several qp values per superblock at a fixed lambda and keeps the cheapest in rate-distortion terms.
options.notes: Library default is 0.

options.description: Distortion measure used inside block decisions. qm-psnr weights errors with the quantization matrix. It works at a lower level than --tune.
options.notes: Library default is psnr. tune=iq and ssimulacra2 switch to qm-psnr.

options.description: Caps the pyramid depth for the GOP that starts at a keyframe. -1 leaves it alone. The effective depth is the smaller of this and --gf-max-pyr-height.
Lets the encoder pick the tile layout from resolution and thread count.
options.notes: Added in 3.10.0. An alternative to setting tile-columns and tile-rows by hand.

options.values: 1: standard (default in good quality and realtime modes), 2: anti-aliased text and graphics aware (default in all intra mode)
options.default: 1 in good quality and realtime modes; 2 in all intra mode
options.description: Chooses how automatic screen-content detection works. Mode 2 also recognizes anti-aliased text and graphics as screen content.

recommendations.why: Mode 2 recognizes anti-aliased text and graphics, which standard detection can miss.

options.notes: Added in 3.13.0. Has no effect when --tune-content=screen forces screen tools anyway.

options.description: Pushes rate-distortion decisions toward keeping sharp coefficients. In all-intra mode it also weakens deblocking.

effect.quality: + detail / sharper lines, may add ringing

recommendations.why: libaom's tune=iq and ssimulacra2 set sharpness 7 as part of their image-quality bundle.

options.notes: Since 3.12.0 it also sets the bitstream loop-filter sharpness in all-intra mode. No source used here tested it for video.

options.description: Varies sharpness with frame quantizer to reduce blocking at low and medium quality. --sharpness then acts as the maximum.

recommendations.why: libaom says it reduces blocking at low and medium quality, and only does anything when sharpness is above 0.

options.notes: Added in 3.13.0. tune=iq turns it on.

options.description: For high-bit-depth encodes, checks that every input sample is valid for the chosen bit depth. Catches 10-bit data that is really 16-bit or 12-bit.
options.notes: Added in 3.14.0. Keep it on: it turns a silent garbled-output bug into an error.

recipes.name: AV1 Pro: 12-bit 4:4:4 archival master (piped)
recipes.goal: Near-transparent 12-bit full-chroma master from a 12-bit RGB/4:4:4 intermediate
recipes.why: 12-bit needs profile 2, but do not pass --profile=2 here: with 12-bit 4:4:4 Y4M that makes aomenc 3.15.3 fail with 'Failed to set chroma subsampling x' (checked locally), while leaving it out lets aomenc raise the profile to 2 itself. A single pass because the input is a stdin pipe. 48 is the largest lookahead 3.15.3 accepts. QM, chroma delta-q and tune=ssim are Codec Wiki's efficiency picks. Change the CICP flags to match the source.

recipes.name: HDR10 PQ 10-bit 4:2:2 intermediate
recipes.why: 4:2:2 needs the Professional profile; an explicit --profile=2 works here at 10-bit (checked locally). PQ/BT.2020 CICP is signaled in-stream. Tile settings follow Codec Wiki's 2160p advice. MaxCLL/MaxFALL and mastering display must be added afterwards with mkvmerge, because aomenc has no flags for them.

recipes.name: HLG 10-bit broadcast-style
recipes.goal: HLG HDR that plays as SDR on non-HDR displays
recipes.why: aomenc's name for HLG is 'hlg'; 'arib-std-b67' is rejected. HLG does not need MDCV/CLL metadata to play correctly.

recipes.name: Heavy film grain with synthesis
recipes.goal: Small files for grainy film without coding the grain
recipes.content: heavy grain, old film, old anime
recipes.why: Codec Wiki's grain level of 8, below its limit of 12. The default --enable-dnl-denoising=1 denoises before coding. Codec Wiki instead turns that off (0), which codes the real grain and layers synthetic grain on top; the sources disagree. Two passes work here because the input is a file.

recipes.name: Camera noise via photon-noise table (HDR)
recipes.goal: Replace sensor noise with matching synthetic noise in a PQ encode
recipes.why: Make noise.tbl with libaom's photon_noise_table example (built from source; Homebrew does not ship it): photon_noise_table --width=3840 --height=2160 --iso=<ISO> -t smpte2084 -o noise.tbl. Feed a denoised source: the table adds synthetic noise but aomenc does not remove the existing noise unless --denoise-noise-level is set.

recipes.name: Anime / 2D animation
recipes.goal: Clean line art and flat colors
recipes.why: Codec Wiki suggests arnr-strength 1 for animation, so the temporal filter does not smear lines. 10-bit prevents banding in flat gradients.

recipes.name: Screen recording / UI
recipes.goal: Sharp text and UI at small size
recipes.why: tune-content=screen turns on palette and intra block copy for every frame instead of relying on detection.

recipes.name: Codec Wiki chunked (Av1an) baseline
recipes.why: Codec Wiki's line for Av1an, with lag-in-frames lowered from its 64 to 48 because 3.15.3 rejects 64. Keyframe options assume Av1an places scene-cut keyframes.
